prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band - draw everything BIGGER than the canvas so parts are literally CROPPED OFF by the edge: the big tube's two rounded end-caps must each be sliced off by a corner of the picture, not shown as complete rounded tips floating inside a white margin, and the same goes for the rope's ends and the thread tangle; (b) there must be NO starburst, no radiating burst, no sparkle rays, no sunbeam rays and no wheel-of-spokes arrangement anywhere in the picture - this is especially important here because the real structure being drawn radiates from a hub, and that idea must be avoided entirely, not softened; (c) use a ZOOMED-IN, DIAGONAL, OVERSIZED composition where long cable-like characters cross the frame corner to corner and run past every edge, so nothing floats in empty white space and nothing arranges itself in a circle or star. Two previous attempts at this same scene left a plain white strip of blank canvas around a fully-visible, fully-contained drawing (tube ends and rope ends fully rounded and floating inside the white margin) - that is exactly what must NOT happen this time. Treat the 1080x1080 canvas as a small window looking at only PART of a much bigger scene: the tube's body must run edge-to-edge from one side of the canvas to the other with its rounded end-caps completely outside the visible canvas (sliced away, not shown at all, on at least one end), and the same for the rope. Zoom in dramatically closer than feels natural - if you can trace a continuous strip of blank white canvas along any of the four edges, the picture has failed; every one of the four edges must be interrupted by black linework at multiple points along its length.

SCENE: Inside a busy, friendly cell, three rope-and-tube characters of different thickness form the cell's scaffolding, muscle and railway all at once - drawn as one big diagonal construction/railway scene, never as spokes meeting at a point.
- The MAIN CHARACTER is one big, chunky, hollow PIPE/TUBE (a microtubule) lying diagonally across the whole square from one corner toward the opposite corner, drawn large enough to dominate the frame. One rounded end of the tube is open and hollow, and that open hollow circle doubles as its big round happy smiling mouth; it has two large simple round eyes with pupils above the opening, and two short stubby cartoon arms with simple mitten hands partway along its body.
- A small round TROLLEY/CART character (a motor protein) with two tiny stubby cartoon legs and a simple friendly dot face stands on top of the big tube partway along its length, as if walking along a railway track, towing a small round wrapped parcel (a vesicle, tied like a little gift-wrapped ball) behind it on a short simple string.
- A second, medium-thick BRAIDED ROPE character (an intermediate filament) - drawn as a twisted candy-cane-like rope with a simple friendly face (two round eyes and a small smile) peeking out partway along it - stretches diagonally across the frame the other way, crossing behind or in front of the big tube, corner to corner, clearly thinner than the big tube but clearly thicker than the thin threads described next.
- Bundled together near one corner of the picture, several EXTRA-THIN WIGGLY THREAD characters (microfilaments) loop and cross each other like a friendly tangle of shoelaces or loose string, clearly the thinnest lines in the whole picture; a couple of them have tiny simple round faces (two dots and a small curved smile) peeking out of the tangle.
- Everything is drawn LARGE, SIMPLE and CHUNKY, with generous open white areas inside every shape so a child can colour them in, and the three characters' line-weights stay visibly different (thinnest threads, medium rope, thickest tube) throughout.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays, or any arrangement of lines/tubes/ropes meeting at a single central point like spokes on a wheel. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere, and NO circular/hub-and-spoke layout at all - describe every fibre as a long cable crossing the frame diagonally instead.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, shelf, table, counter or vignette. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square - the tube, the rope and the thread tangle are all CUT OFF by the image edge itself.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO DNA double-helix, no chromosome shapes, no bacterial corkscrew/flagellum shape anywhere.
- NO human figures, no real flames, no arrows, nothing being squashed, hurt or destroyed unkindly - this is a cheerful railway-and-scaffolding scene, not a demolition scene.
